A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Sparse PCA framework. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison across revisions and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original runtime and objective-value experiments with Branch-and-Bound and Chan’s algorithm, including detailed results and parameter analyses in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 reports revised real-data experiments, support diagnostics, synthetic simulations, and parameter analyses in Section 5 and Appendix C.

M1.justification: Algorithms 2–3 now extract original principal submatrices A[S,S] after identifying blocks through thresholding, instead of solving on thresholded submatrices. Candidate selection also changes from the thresholded objective to the original objective. This changes block optimization itself; v1’s appendix PCA refinement only refitted an already selected support.

E1.justification: Appendix C.4 adds explicitly generated Gaussian block-covariance data under Model 1, extending the synthetic evaluation beyond the noisy-block illustration retained from v1. All eleven real-data covariance datasets and the Sparse PCA task remain.

E2.justification: Branch-and-Bound and Chan’s algorithm remain the evaluated baselines. The new simulation also uses Branch-and-Bound. No additional external comparison method is evaluated; the other algorithms in Table 1 remain theoretical comparisons.

E3.justification: Appendix C.1 replaces dataset-specific Branch-and-Bound settings with a common search range, changes d0 from 40 to 30, and standardizes delta to 0.01 times the matrix infinity norm. Early stopping becomes a general experimental instruction. v2 also introduces support-overlap diagnostics and a synthetic protocol with different sparsity values and a 600-second baseline limit.

E4.justification: v2 adds support-overlap, threshold, and sparsity analyses and a simulation checking Proposition 2’s bound. The LymphomaCov2 block-size analysis is revised from d0=40/50/60 to 30/45/55. The combined ArceneCov refinement comparison is removed, while a separate ProstateCov tolerance sensitivity analysis is added.

E5.justification: Appendix C.4 newly specifies seed 42 and ten runs per sparsity value, with run-based standard deviations in Table 12. Both versions already report standard deviations across real-data experimental cases; v2 does not establish increased repetitions for those retained experiments.

E6.justification: Tables 3–4 change reported average speedup/error from 93.77/2.15% to 100.50/0.61% for Branch-and-Bound and from 6.77/0.37% to 6.00/-0.91% for Chan’s algorithm. Detailed runtimes, objectives, errors, and parameter-study results also change, and diagnostic and simulation results are added. These shifts accompany method and protocol revisions, so they are not controlled same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Theorems 3–4 reduce the threshold penalty from (1+1/m) times k epsilon to k epsilon/m. v2 explicitly adds symmetry and positive-semidefiniteness assumptions, revises Model 1’s conditions and Proposition 2’s bound, and substantially develops Theorem 4’s proof in Appendix B.3. Appendix D adds a conditional extension to non-positive-semidefinite inputs.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution summary newly emphasize that integration often finds better solutions than Chan’s algorithm, replacing the earlier headline of a small positive average approximation loss. The principal novelty, plug-and-play framework, and asymptotic acceleration claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of support overlap and threshold behavior, and explains that non-positive-semidefinite applicability depends on the chosen subroutine. It removes v1’s explicit main-text underperformance caveat and detailed ArceneCov runtime explanation, while retaining revised discussions of parameter-dependent accuracy/runtime tradeoffs.

D1.justification: v2 revises hyperparameter and early-stopping instructions, omits the earlier support-PCA refinement description, and supplies a synthetic-data generation recipe. Hardware remains unchanged. Reproducibility of the new simulation is limited by C.4’s ambiguous references to the noisy matrix A versus the clean matrix A-tilde as solver input.

R1.justification: Appendix A adds graphical-lasso decomposition work by Mazumder and Hastie (2012), Fattahi and Sojoudi (2019), and Wang et al. (2023). This expands the discussion of related decomposition techniques while retaining the existing Sparse PCA novelty positioning.

P1.justification: v2 makes focused prose and notation edits, adds acknowledgements, reorganizes the appendix’s parameter discussions, and introduces new appendix subsections. The main narrative and section sequence remain largely intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn to preserve original within-block entries and its caption is revised. New diagnostic, simulation, and tolerance tables substantially expand the empirical presentation. Existing tables are integrated more closely with their discussions, the block-size table is revised and relocated, and the old ArceneCov refinement table is removed.

improvement.justification: The central gain is the revised block construction: original principal submatrices preserve covariance structure and support tighter guarantees than v1’s thresholded-block procedure. More explicit proofs and support/sensitivity analyses substantially strengthen justification and assessability. These benefits outweigh the reduced failure discussion and remaining simulation/reporting ambiguities. The revised headline scores involve changed settings and are not themselves evidence of an overall quality improvement.
